summary: This note is a collection of passages on the Ottoman Empire, founded in 1299 by Osman I and dissolved in 1922. It covers the empire's origins and name, territorial expansion under rulers such as Suleiman the Magnificent, military and state organisation, naval history, economy, culture, demographic shifts and migrations, and its collapse after World War I.
one_line: Overview of the Ottoman Empire (1299–1922): founding, expansion, institutions, military, economy, culture, demographic change, and collapse after World War I.
key_facts: The Ottoman Empire was founded in 1299 by Oghuz Turks under Osman I in northwestern Anatolia.
Mehmed the Conqueror ended the Byzantine Empire with the 1453 conquest of Constantinople.
Suleiman the Magnificent (1520–1566) captured Belgrade in 1521, won the Battle of Mohács in 1526, and besieged Vienna in 1529 without taking it.
In the Battle of Ankara in 1402, Timur defeated the Ottomans and captured Sultan Bayezid I, starting a civil war that lasted until 1413, when Mehmed I emerged as sultan.
The Armistice of Mudros was signed on 30 October 1918; the sultanate was abolished on 1 November 1922 and the caliphate on 3 March 1924.
The last sultan, Mehmed VI (reigned 1918–22), left the country on 17 November 1922.
The Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca of 1774 ended the Russo-Turkish War of 1768–1774 and gave freedom to worship to Christians in Wallachia and Moldavia.
By 1914, only 19.1% of the empire's population was non-Muslim, mostly Greeks, Assyrians, Armenians, and Jews.
In 1911, 528 of the 654 wholesale companies in Istanbul were owned by ethnic Greeks.
Between 1783 and 1913, approximately 5–7 million refugees entered the Ottoman Empire, at least 3.8 million from Russia.
Beginning in 1320 a Grand Vizier was appointed, and from the late 16th century he became the de facto head of state as sultans withdrew from politics.
Sultan Abdülhamid II locked most of the fleet in the Golden Horn, where the ships decayed for 30 years; the Ottoman Navy Foundation was established in 1910 to buy ships through public donations.
The main corps of the Ottoman Army included Janissary, Sipahi, Akıncı and Mehterân.
At the beginning of the 17th century the empire contained 32 provinces and numerous vassal states.
